[https://www.ravenprotocol.com/]
Ravnest — Distributed Deep Learning Training Distributed Deep Learning Training Framework Train complex deep learning models across heterogeneous consumer-grade PCs connected via the internet. Ravnest combines data and model parallelism with a novel asynchronous training approach. View on GitHub Read the Paper Documentation Architecture How It Works Ravnest orchestrates distributed training through a four-stage pipeline that handles cluster formation, parallel training, global synchronization, and fault recovery. 01 01 Matchmaking & Cluster Formation Requester and compute nodes connect to an intermediary matchmaking server that profiles each node's hardware capabilities and network characteristics. Nodes are algorithmically grouped into clusters with similar data transfer rates and compute power, minimizing intra-cluster communication overhead. The model is then fragmented into submodels distributed across the cluster. 02 02 Zero-Bubble Asynchronous Model Parallel Training Within each cluster, the model is partitioned across nodes using model parallelism. A zero-bubble pipeline schedule feeds micro-batches through the pipeline stages asynchronously, ensuring no node sits idle waiting for forward or backward passes from adjacent stages. This eliminates the pipeline bubble problem that plagues synchronous pipeline parallelism. Fig 1a — Naive model parallelism: large idle time bubble as each device waits for the previous stage. Fig 1b — Pipeline parallelism with micro-batches: overlapping forward and backward passes shrinks the bubble. 03 03 Parallel Multi-Ring All-Reduce After local training iterations within clusters, global parameter averaging is performed using a parallel multi-ring all-reduce algorithm. This distributes the communication load evenly across all nodes, avoiding the bottleneck of a centralized parameter server. Synchronization is triggered periodically rather than after every iteration, amortizing communication cost. Fig 2a — One round of Ring All-Reduce: scatter-reduce followed by all-gather across nodes A, B, and C. Fig 2b — Parallel Multi-Ring All-Reduce: 5 parallel rings distribute communication load during global parameter averaging. 04 04 Fault Recovery & Dynamic Scaling New peers can join ongoing training sessions at any time. Based on fault tolerance requirements, they either join existing clusters as backup nodes — mapped to the least reliable node with extra communication channels for seamless failover — or form entirely new clusters. This enables continuous training even as nodes drop in and out. Under the Hood Technical Deep Dive The core algorithms and techniques that power Ravnest's distributed training. Nodes are algorithmically grouped into clusters with similar data transfer rates and compute power, minimizing intra-cluster communication overhead and maximizing training throughput. leads.posting: Exclusive: Gramiyaa raises fresh capital in Series A round at Rs 110 Cr valuation. Bengaluru-based cold-pressed oil brand Gramiyaa has raised Rs 18.65 crore in a Series A funding round led by new investor Optiscape Network Holdings and participation from existing investors Homegrown Ventures, Campus Fund and others. In March 2025, the company had raised Rs 7.2 crore in a pre-Series A round led by Homegrown Ventures, with participation from Campus Fund and Mumbai Angels. According to its regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr , the company ’s board has allotted 32,968 Series A CCPS at Rs 5,657 per share to raise the fresh capital. Optiscape Network Holdings led the round with an investment of Rs 9 crore, followed by Homegrown Ventures with Rs 4.5 crore and Campus Fund with Rs 4 crore. Sarya Global Holdings invested Rs 90 lakh, while Rasagna Pulapaka contributed Rs 25 lakh in the round. As per Entrackr’s estimates, Gramiyaa’s valuation surged 49% to Rs 110 crore in Series A from Rs 74 crore in the pre-Series A round. The proceeds will be deployed towards growth capital and other general corporate requirements Founded in 2016 by Sibi Manivannan, Gramiyaa is a cold-pressed oil brand that makes its products in-house using traditional oil-making methods. The D2C company offers groundnut, coconut, sesame and mustard oils, along with virgin coconut and olive oils, and sells through its own website as well as platforms such as Amazon, Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart, BigBasket, DMart Ready and FirstClub. After the latest allotment, Homegrown Ventures remains the largest external shareholder with a 17.34% stake, followed by Campus Fund at 9.86% and Optiscape Network Holdings at 8.28%. Meanwhile, C c o-founders Sibi Manivannan, Mohamed Yaseen and Naveenrajaman RL hold retained 26.04%, 13.02% and 13.02%, respectively. The company is yet to file its FY26 financials. In FY25, Gramiyaa’s revenue jumped 72.7% YoY to Rs 19 crore, while its losses surged nearly 12.7X to Rs 4 crore.
